title: Albert Sabin, born to Jewish parents from Poland, developed an oral polio vaccine that nearly eradicated the disease

trailer.text: Albert Sabin, a Polish-American medical researcher, is best known for developing the oral polio vaccine.
He was born to Jewish parents in Poland in 1906. In 1931 he received his M.D. from New York University and immediately began research on polio.
He isolated attenuated strains of the virus. Before trying them on others, he and his associates swallowed them themselves.
The vaccine was given by mouth and was cheap and easy to administer.
Since it came into wide use, polio has virtually been eradicated from the Western Hemisphere.

stations.title: From Bialystok to New York, in the years of polio fear

paragraphs.text: Albert Sabin was born on August 26, 1906, in Bialystok, Poland, to Jewish parents.
According to Aish, his family, like many Jews, faced intense anti-Semitism, and the threat of violence was never far away.
The family emigrated to the United States to escape the persecution of Jews.
According to the Smithsonian, Sabin and Jonas Salk were two young Jewish men from the New York area, both drawn to medical studies, who did not know each other at the time.
In the first half of the 20th century, Americans lived in fear of polio.
It is a paralytic disease that was not understood, and no one knew how to contain it.
Many hospitals refused to admit patients who were believed to have contracted polio.
By the early 1950s, 25,000 to 50,000 people were becoming infected with polio each year, and in 1952, 3,000 died from it.
According to one source, in the '50s up to about 16 thousand people were paralyzed each year, most of them children.
The iron lungs saved lives, but became an intimidating visual reminder of what the disease does.
In 1931 Sabin received his M.D. from New York University and immediately began research on polio.
Sabin and Peter Olitsky discovered that polio does not enter the human body through the nose, as had previously been suggested.
In 1940 Sabin and his assistants traveled to morgues in Ohio, Indiana and West Virginia.
There they performed autopsies on every polio victim they could.
In Cincinnati, Sabin found that the virus not only grew in nervous tissue, but also lived in the small intestine.
From this he resolved to make the human gut a hostile environment for the virus.
The way to do this was to isolate a mutant strain of the virus that was incapable of causing the disease.
The experiments involved approximately nine thousand monkeys and more than one hundred chimpanzees, and they enabled him to isolate rare mutant polioviruses.
By 1957 he had identified three attenuated strains that were ready for small trials in humans.
According to the March of Dimes foundation, from 1952 to 1961 Sabin received about $1.5 million for polio research.
Before trying the live, non-dangerous viruses on others, Sabin and his research associates swallowed them themselves.
In 1957 a small group of volunteers, including Sabin's wife and children, received the vaccine, and the results were encouraging.
According to Smithsonian, Sabin conducted trials on prisoners at a federal prison in Chillicothe, Ohio.
According to Smithsonian, all thirty prisoners developed antibodies, and none of them fell ill.
According to TIME, Sabin reported only one setback: some of the virus changed in the subjects' bodies to a somewhat virulent form.

Also according to TIME, to support his claim that a live virus gives longer-lasting immunity, Sabin relied on one of the isolated communities of the Eskimos, in which immunity against polio was found to have lasted 40 years after the last encounter with the virus.

stations.title: The large trials, far from home, and in Israel too

paragraphs.text: Sabin was ready for large-scale trials, but he could not carry them out in the United States.
According to Smithsonian, he tested the vaccine in Russia, East Germany and smaller Soviet Bloc countries.
According to the University of Cincinnati, Mikhail Chumakov tested the vaccine on 10 million children in Russia in 1959.
According to the University of Cincinnati, this trial proved that the oral vaccine was safe.
Sabin came from Cincinnati to Israel to advise the health authorities on the use of the vaccine.
According to JTA, the Ministry of Health reported that the first experiments with the live vaccine in Israel had been conducted successfully in two collective settlements.
In two kibbutzim, half of the children were given live vaccine and the other half pure water.
No one suffered side effects, and the vaccine also infected and immunized others who had not been vaccinated.
Ministry of Health officials indicated that Israel would not replace the Salk vaccine with the live vaccine as long as information on it was not coordinated by the World Health Organization.

stations.title: A spoonful of cherry syrup in Cincinnati

paragraphs.text: In Cincinnati, children received a spoonful of cherry-flavored syrup with drops of the vaccine, instead of an injection.
According to the Cincinnati library, over eight days in April–May 1960, about 80,000 preschool-age children in the city received a free dose of the vaccine.
According to the library, following the campaign the polio virus was eradicated from the city's population.
The vaccine was taken by mouth and needed no follow-up doses.
It is cheaper and easier to administer, and therefore more suitable for mass immunization campaigns.
According to EBSCO, between 1970 and 1990 the oral vaccine prevented an estimated 5 million cases of paralysis worldwide.
In the United States the number of paralysis cases dropped sharply, to an average of fewer than ten per year.
In 1994 polio was declared eradicated from the Americas, thanks to the two vaccines.

According to Aish, after Sabin was diagnosed in 1983 with ascending paralysis and the Chicago Tribune published his address, more than 100,000 people wrote to him, and schoolchildren volunteered to help him count the letters and reply to them.
According to Aish, school children volunteered to help him count the letters and reply to them.
The success brought Sabin many honors at home and abroad.
In 1970 he received the National Medal of Science from President Nixon.
The official award citation stated that his vaccine eliminated polio as a major threat to human health.
In 1986 Ronald Reagan awarded him the Presidential Medal of Freedom, and in the same year he received the Soviet Union's Order of Friendship Among Peoples for the vaccine.
In 2012 he was named a "Great Ohioan".
Aish claims that neither Salk nor Sabin patented the vaccines, even though a patent could have made them very wealthy.

stations.title: In Rehovot, and to the end of the road

paragraphs.text: Sabin served as President of the Weizmann Institute of Science.
He was the first president of the institute required to be a scientist himself.
Sabin became an advocate for peace and fought the diseases of ignorance and poverty.
In 1983 Sabin developed an illness that left him paralyzed.
He died on March 3, 1993.
That same year, upon Sabin's death, longtime friends and colleagues established the Sabin Vaccine Institute, led by his widow, Heloisa Sabin, and Dr. H.R. Shepherd, the founding chairman.
Heloisa died on October 12, 2016.
According to Aish, he was diagnosed with ascending paralysis

stations.title: The risk, and the dispute with Salk

paragraphs.text: Occasionally the live virus in the vaccine reverts to a disease-causing form and may cause paralysis in the vaccinated person.
In 1999 the U.S. government recommended a return to the injected vaccine.
The aim was to avoid any chance of a recipient contracting polio from the attenuated virus in the Sabin vaccine.
The rival vaccine also had failures. The Salk vaccine was accidentally contaminated with live virulent polioviruses, which brought death or severe illness to hundreds of school children.
According to AAI, in the Cutter incident 56 children developed paralysis, and five of them died.
In 1973 Salk denounced Sabin's vaccine as unsafe and tried to persuade the public to return to his own vaccine.
According to Smithsonian, it is Salk who is credited with ending the scourge of polio, because his vaccine was first to market.

disagreements.question: In what year did the Sabin family emigrate to the United States?

versions.says: According to the Sabin Vaccine Institute, the family emigrated to the United States in 1921
According to the University of Cincinnati timeline, the family remained in Bialystok until 1920, and then made the arduous journey to the United States

disagreements.question: How many prisoners took part in the first trials?

versions.says: According to Smithsonian, thirty prisoners at the prison in Chillicothe, and all of them developed antibodies
According to AAI, the first trial, in the winter of 1954–55, was on 30 prisoners at a federal prison in Ohio
According to TIME in 1955, of 30 volunteers at a prison in Ohio, 26 got a minute droplet of a single strain of the virus
According to an encyclopedia, in 1955–1957 Sabin gave the vaccine to hundreds of prison inmates, with no harmful side effects

disagreements.question: How many people were vaccinated in the Soviet Union and elsewhere?

versions.says: According to AAI, Sabin convinced the Soviet Union to allow a field trial with 10 million participants, five times larger than the Salk trial, with no control group
According to the University of Cincinnati, 10 million children in Russia in 1959
According to an encyclopedia, about 145 million people in the Soviet Union by 1960

disagreements.question: How many children were vaccinated in Cincinnati in 1960?

versions.says: According to the Cincinnati library, about 80,000 preschool-age children over eight days in April–May
According to the University of Cincinnati, over 20,000 children on April 24, and within two weeks over 180,000 children in the region

disagreements.question: When was the vaccine licensed in the United States, or when did it become standard?

versions.says: According to an encyclopedia, the vaccine became available to the public in 1961, after four years of tests around the world
According to EBSCO, in 1962 all three strains were licensed for general use by the United States Public Health Service
According to Smithsonian, in 1963 the vaccine became the standard vaccine, and the one used in the worldwide effort to eradicate polio

disagreements.question: When did Sabin serve as president of the Weizmann Institute?

versions.says: According to the Sabin Vaccine Institute, from 1970 to 1972
According to an encyclopedia, he was appointed in 1972 and left the position two years later

claims.quote: Albert Bruce Sabin was born to Jewish parents in Poland in 1906 and came to the United States in 1921

claims.text: סבין קיבל תואר דוקטור לרפואה מאוניברסיטת ניו יורק ב-1931 ומיד החל לחקור את הפוליו.

claims.text: הוא התכוון לעשות זאת באמצעות בידוד זן מוטנטי של נגיף הפוליו שאינו מסוגל לגרום למחלה.
claims.quote: This he intended to accomplish by isolating a mutant form of the polio virus that was incapable of producing the disease.

claims.text: עד 1957 זיהה סבין שלושה זני נגיף מוחלשים שהיו מוכנים לניסויים קטנים בבני אדם.
claims.quote: By 1957, Sabin had identified three strains of attenuated viruses that were ready for small experimental trials in humans.

claims.text: סבין ושותפיו למחקר בלעו בעצמם את הנגיפים החיים הלא-מסוכנים לפני שניסו אותם על אחרים.
claims.quote: Sabin and his research associates first ingested the live avirulent viruses themselves before they experimented on other human subjects.

claims.text: החיסון של סבין ניתן דרך הפה ולא נזקק למנות מעקב.
claims.quote: Sabin’s vaccine could be taken orally and never needed any follow-up doses.

claims.text: החיסון הפומי זול וקל יותר למתן, ולכן מתאים יותר לקמפיינים של חיסון המוני.
claims.quote: The oral vaccine is cheaper and is easier to administer; therefore, it is more suitable for mass immunization campaigns.

claims.text: מאז שהחיסון נכנס לשימוש נרחב, הפוליו כמעט הוכחד בחצי הכדור המערבי.
claims.quote: Since it became widely used, polio has virtually been eradicated from the Western Hemisphere.

claims.text: סבין נולד ב-26 באוגוסט 1906 בביאליסטוק שבפולין.

claims.text: לעיתים הנגיף החי מתמוטט לצורה גורמת מחלה ועלול לגרום לשיתוק אצל המחוסן.
claims.quote: Occasionally, the live virus mutates to a disease-causing (virulent) form as it multiplies in the vaccinated person.

claims.text: ממשלת ארצות הברית המליצה ב-1999 לחזור לחיסון המוזרק כדי למנוע סיכוי שמחוסן ידבק בפוליו מהנגיף המוחלש בחיסון של סבין.
claims.quote: the U.S. government recommended a return to IPV in 1999 to avoid any chance of a recipient contracting polio from the attenuated virus in the Sabin vaccine

claims.text: חיסון סולק זוהם בטעות בנגיפי פוליו חיים ואלימים, שגרמו למוות או למחלה קשה למאות ילדי בית ספר.
claims.quote: was accidently contaminated with some live virulent polioviruses which subsequently brought death or severe illness to several hundred school children

claims.text: לפי AAI, באירוע קאטר 56 ילדים פיתחו שיתוק, וחמישה מהם מתו.
claims.quote: Worse, 56 children developed the paralytic form of the disease, resulting in five deaths.

claims.text: סולק גינה ב-1973 את החיסון של סבין כבלתי בטוח וניסה לשכנע את הציבור לחזור לחיסון שלו.
claims.quote: in 1973 as being unsafe and tried to persuade the public to use his vaccine again

claims.text: לפי סמיתסוניאן, סולק מקבל את הקרדיט על סיום מכת הפוליו משום שחיסונו יצא ראשון לשוק.
claims.quote: Although Jonas Salk is credited with ending the scourge of polio because his killed-virus vaccine was first to market

claims.text: לפי ציר הזמן של אוניברסיטת סינסינטי, משפחת סבין נשארה בביאליסטוק עד 1920 ואז עשתה את המסע המפרך לארצות הברית.
claims.quote: Albert Sabin’s family remained in Bialystok until 1920 when they made the arduous journey to join the rest of their family in the United States.

claims.text: לפי AAI, הניסוי הראשון של סבין, בחורף 1954–55, נערך על 30 אסירים בכלא פדרלי באוהיו.
claims.quote: Sabin’s first trial, in the winter of 1954–55, was on 30 prisoners at the United States Industrial Reformatory in Chilicothe, Ohio

claims.text: לפי טיים ב-1955, מתוך 30 מתנדבים בכלא באוהיו קיבלו 26 טיפה זעירה מזן אחד של נגיף הפוליו.
claims.quote: Of 30 volunteers (between the ages of 21 and 30), 26 got a minute droplet of a single strain of polio virus

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה, בשנים 1955–1957 נתן סבין את החיסון למאות אסירים ללא תופעות לוואי מזיקות.
claims.quote: For two years (1955-1957) he gave the vaccine to hundreds of prison inmates with no harmful effects.

claims.text: לפי AAI, שנתיים אחר כך שכנע סבין את ברית המועצות לאפשר ניסוי שדה גדול פי חמישה מניסוי סולק, עם 10 מיליון משתתפים ללא קבוצת ביקורת.
claims.quote: Sabin was able to convince the Soviet Union to allow a field trial of his live-virus vaccine using five times the number of children involved in the Salk trial

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה, הבדיקות המוצלחות בברית המועצות הגיעו לכ-145 מיליון איש עד 1960.
claims.quote: The highly successful vaccination tests in the Soviet Union reached about 145 million people by 1960.

claims.text: לפי אוניברסיטת סינסינטי, ב-24 באפריל 1960 קיבלו יותר מ-20,000 ילדים את החיסון, ותוך שבועיים יותר מ-180,000 ילדי האזור.
claims.quote: Within two weeks, over 180,000 of the region's children ages 3 months to 6 years received the vaccine.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה, החיסון הפך זמין לציבור ב-1961 לאחר ארבע שנות ניסויים ברחבי העולם.
claims.quote: It became available to the public in 1961 following four years of worldwide tests.

claims.text: לפי EBSCO, ב-1962 הורשו כל שלושת הזנים של סבין לשימוש כללי על ידי שירות הבריאות הציבורי האמריקאי.
claims.quote: In 1962, after four years of deliberation by the United States Public Health Service, all three of Sabin’s vaccine strains were licensed for general use.

claims.text: לפי סמיתסוניאן, ב-1963 הפך החיסון של סבין לחיסון הסטנדרטי ולזה ששימש במאמץ למגר את הפוליו בעולם.
claims.quote: In 1963, it became the standard vaccine, and the one used in the effort to eradicate polio around the world.

claims.text: לפי Aish, לא סולק ולא סבין רשמו פטנט על החיסונים, אף שהיו יכולים להתעשר.
claims.quote: Neither Jonas Salk nor Albert Sabin ever patented their vaccines, even though doing so could have made them unimaginably wealthy.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה, סבין מונה לנשיא מכון ויצמן בישראל ב-1972 ועזב את התפקיד שנתיים לאחר מכן.
claims.quote: He was appointed president of the Weizmann Institute in Israel in 1972. Although he left that position two years later

claims.text: אלברט סבין, חוקר רפואי פולני-אמריקאי, ידוע בעיקר כמי שפיתח את חיסון הפוליו הפומי.
claims.quote: best known for developing the live, orally-administered vaccine

claims.text: אלברט סבין, חוקר רפואי פולני-אמריקאי, ידוע בעיקר כמי שפיתח את חיסון הפוליו הפומי.
claims.quote: the development of the oral polio vaccine

claims.text: ב-1986 העניק לו רונלד רייגן את מדליית החירות הנשיאותית, ובאותה שנה קיבל על החיסון את עיטור ידידות העמים של ברית המועצות.
claims.quote: The Presidential Medal of Freedom was given to Dr. Sabin by Ronald Reagan in 1986

claims.text: ב-1986 העניק לו רונלד רייגן את מדליית החירות הנשיאותית, ובאותה שנה קיבל על החיסון את עיטור ידידות העמים של ברית המועצות.
claims.quote: Order of the Friendship Among Peoples Medal in 1986, its highest civilian honor.

claims.text: ב-1983 חלה סבין במחלה שגרמה לו שיתוק.
claims.quote: After Sabin developed calcification of the cervical spine in 1983
